# The Disruptor

> The Disruptor is a free, open-source simulation of running the innovation portfolio of a company, built for teaching corporate entrepreneurship and innovation management. The player is the new Chief Innovation Officer (CIO) of a Belgian fitness equipment firm and makes consequential decisions under uncertainty across a three-year tenure, answering to a board that expects results. It runs in the browser with nothing to install, no account and no student data collected; a full three-year run takes between 45 minutes and an hour and a half, depending on the player’s experience and engagement. It was created by Ammon Salter (Warwick Business School, University of Warwick) and built through AI-assisted development.

The player arrives as the new CIO of Vélox Dynamics, a fictional Belgian fitness-equipment company in Vilvoorde, trying to reinvent itself. Each week, decisions arrive in a central cockpit: project proposals, events, warnings, staff requests, competitor moves, board nudges. Their consequences work back through the firm. The role spans a connected set of managerial practices rather than a string of isolated frameworks: setting innovation strategy, running an R&D portfolio across three horizons, launching innovations, building and leading teams, shaping organisation and culture, negotiating alliances and open innovation, running a platform, managing intellectual property, scouting the outside world, working with universities, investing in start-ups, crowdsourcing ideas, engaging with standards, chasing grants, and responding to competitors. The systems interact, so there is no single winning strategy; causal ambiguity is a deliberate design goal, and the same approach produces different outcomes on different playthroughs.

The simulation is grounded in innovation and corporate entrepreneurship research. Around twenty-five concepts from the literature are embedded in its systems, including absorptive capacity, organisational ambidexterity, appropriability and value capture, creative destruction, diffusion of innovations, dominant design, dynamic capabilities, systems of innovation, open innovation, path dependence, platform strategy, structural holes and VRIN resources. A Pantheon of real innovation scholars brings up the relevant idea in context as players face each dilemma. Students experience these concepts through decisions rather than reading about them.

The Forge is the core game, played as a full three-year tenure or a one-year probation that can lead on to the full term; three harder versions, still marked experimental, change the conditions: Pivot (move the company into a new sector), Jugaad (frugal innovation with far less money and no inherited projects) and Gauntlet (hostile markets and competitors who strike early). A teaching variant, the Incubator, starts players with two systems open and lets them open the rest one at a time, at the pace of a syllabus, with the board not ending the appointment over a poor record, so first-time players can experiment freely. Three short arcade mini-games sit inside the simulation. Version 2 adds the management board in person (it meets each year on the firm's direction and the CEO decides), an end-of-year appraisal after the first and second years, choices about how far generative AI goes in R&D, and a new ending: a report, "Your tenure at Vélox", that sets the board's view of the results beside the game's own assessment of how the player used the tools of corporate entrepreneurship and innovation management. A comparison with other players' results is planned for the Forge version. The game's content is free under a Creative Commons BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence and its software under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, with no accounts and no student data collected. A free educator pack (a teaching note with deployment formats and debrief prompts, an exam question bank, a student onboarding sheet, an introduction slide deck, and the Vélox Dynamics teaching case) is available on request from ammon.salter@wbs.ac.uk.

## Play

- [Play The Disruptor](https://disruptorsim.org/play/): the game itself, in the browser, free.

## For educators

- [For Educators](https://disruptorsim.org/educators.html): who the game is for, learning objectives, the concepts it teaches, the Incubator teaching mode, six ways to use it in class, a ninety-minute class worked through, and how to request the free educator pack.
- [How to Play](https://disruptorsim.org/how-to-play.html): quick start, tutorials, how time flows, the first weeks, the money, the board's year, how an appointment can end early, saving, and the end of a tenure.
- [The Vélox World](https://disruptorsim.org/case-study.html): the teaching case study behind the game's fictional company and industry setting.

## Background

- [About](https://disruptorsim.org/about.html): what the game is, the experience, the managerial practices and systems, what is new in Version 2, a tenure from start to end, the versions side by side, and how a tenure ends.
- [Licence](https://disruptorsim.org/licence.html): content CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, software PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 — educational use is free; commercial use needs a separate licence.
- [Source code](https://github.com/ammonsalter-del/thedisruptor-sim): the open-source repository.
- [FAQ](https://disruptorsim.org/faq.html): 64 questions in five groups (players, educators, the game and its versions, technical and practical, licence and citing): the board, the money, AI, dismissal, the versions, the Incubator, saving, offline play, assessment and citation.
- Citation for the current version: Salter, A. (2026). The Disruptor: A Corporate Entrepreneurship & Innovation Simulation (Version 2.0.0) [Software]. Warwick Business School, University of Warwick. https://disruptorsim.org
- [Archived release of Version 1.0.2](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21127039): Salter, A. (2026). The Disruptor: An Innovation Management and Corporate Entrepreneurship Simulation (Version 1.0.2) [Software]. Zenodo.
